questions.text: In a hospital, mall, and school case study, which source-safe first step controls?

options.text: Classify each facility or component by actual use before applying fire and egress rules.
Apply one public-building answer to all three.
Start with discount and VAT rules even when no source was checked.
Use BP 344 dimensions without a raw-source gate.

questions.rationale: The checked RA 9514 and PD 1096 sources classify hospitals, malls, schools, restaurants, storage, and mixed occupancies by actual use.

questions.text: Under checked RA 9514 text, which occupancy includes hospitals?
questions.rationale: RA 9514 health care facilities include hospitals, nursing homes, and birth centers.
questions.explanation: Tests RA 9442 priority service obligations applied specifically to the hospital setting.

questions.text: Under checked RA 9514 text, which occupancy includes malls and department stores?
questions.rationale: RA 9514 mercantile occupancies include malls, supermarkets, department stores, and shopping centers.
questions.explanation: Tests accessible parking stall dimensions and the connection requirement — mall-specific application of BP 344.
questions.code_citation: BP 344 – Mall Module, accessible parking provisions

questions.text: Under checked RA 9514 text, which occupancy includes schools used by six or more persons for instruction?
questions.rationale: RA 9514 educational occupancies include buildings or portions used by six or more persons for instruction, including schools.
questions.explanation: Tests the BP 344 requirement for accessible alternatives to escalators — a fundamental principle in the mall module.

questions.text: What does RA 9514 mixed occupancy require when two or more occupancy classes are intermingled and separate safeguards are impracticable?

options.text: Egress sufficient for each room or section and safeguards meeting the most stringent requirements involved.
Only the least restrictive occupancy rules.
No egress review until after occupancy.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 mixed-occupancy provisions require egress for each room or section and the most stringent safeguards of the occupancies involved.
questions.explanation: Tests RA 10754 commercial discount provisions — confirms the 20% + 12% VAT rate applies to mall tenants, not only to medical services.

questions.text: For an educational room or space, when does checked RA 9514 require at least two doorways?

options.text: When capacity is fifty or more persons or area is over 93 sqm.
Only when the school has more than four storeys.
Only when the room has fixed seats.
Never; educational rooms use one doorway.

questions.rationale: RA 9514 requires at least two doorways for educational rooms or spaces with capacity of fifty or more persons or over 93 sqm in area.
questions.explanation: Tests the RA 7277 education right and its physical design implications for school buildings.

questions.text: What is the checked RA 9514 travel-distance limit for educational buildings without approved supervised sprinklers?
questions.rationale: RA 9514 limits educational building travel distance to 46 m without approved supervised automatic sprinkler protection.
questions.explanation: Scenario-based question tracing a complete accessible route through a school building — tests integration of multiple BP 344 dimensions.
questions.code_citation: BP 344 – School Module; Appendix A Sec 1.2.a; Appendix B

questions.text: What is the checked RA 9514 travel-distance limit for educational buildings protected throughout by an approved supervised sprinkler system?
questions.rationale: RA 9514 permits travel distance up to 61 m in educational buildings protected throughout by an approved supervised automatic sprinkler system.
questions.explanation: Tests curb ramp specifications as applied to hospital drop-off zones — distinguishes curb ramp standards from full ramp standards.
questions.code_citation: BP 344 – Hospital Module, drop-off zone provisions

questions.text: Which PD 1096 anchor is source-safe for a public hospital parking check?

options.text: The checked table includes a public hospital row under Division D-2.
Use the boarding-house bed row for all hospitals.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 includes a checked public hospital row under Division D-2 in the parking/loading table.
questions.explanation: Tests the RA 10754 hospital discount provisions — a direct recall question on financial privileges in the hospital setting.

questions.text: Which Fire Code statement is safe for all three case-study facilities?

options.text: Exits must be appropriate to occupancy, occupant count, fire protection, height, and construction type.
One exit rule applies equally to hospital, mall, and school.
Accessibility discount law determines exit capacity.
Parking count is the only life-safety control.

questions.rationale: The Fire Code source family requires exits appropriate to the individual building or structure and its occupancy conditions.
questions.explanation: Comparative evaluation across all three case study building types — tests nuanced understanding of how RA 10754 applies differently to educational fees.

questions.text: Which answer correctly excludes unsupported material from this Batch 065 case study?

options.text: Do not use BP 344, RA 9442, RA 10754, discount, VAT, or curb-ramp dimensions unless those source families are separately raw-audited.
Use all accessibility and VAT claims because the project is public-facing.
Assume mall tenants determine hospital occupancy.
Replace fire classification with service-priority rules.

questions.rationale: Batch 065 selected PD 1096, RA 9514, and PD 9514 raw-source families; unsupported accessibility and discount claims are excluded from this local-first rewrite.
questions.explanation: Tests the PD 1096 occupancy classification of hospitals and its accessibility implications versus commercial occupancies.
